habitat: Usually in pairs in bushveld, suburbia, large exotic trees and rocky hillsides. It perches on buildings and street lights and feeds on lawns at night.
summary: A very common resident. A fairly large grey-brown owl with prominent ear tufts, pale yellow eyes and lightly blotched, finely barred underparts. A less common rufous morph has orange-yellow eyes. The male calls hu-hooo and the female hu-hu-hooo. The Kemp name Spotted Eagle Owl and the code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Cape Eagle-Owl is larger, with orange-yellow eyes, heavily blotched underparts, bold barring and larger feet.

head.pattern: Prominent ear tufts and a dark border to the facial disc. The eyes are pale yellow.

upperparts.pattern: Dark brown above. The description calls the bird grey-brown.

underparts.pattern: Lightly blotched underparts with fine barring of dark brown, white and buff.

head.pattern: Prominent ear tufts. The less common rufous morph has orange-yellow eyes.

underparts.pattern: Fine barring separates the rufous morph from Cape Eagle-Owl.

viewNotes.note: Pale yellow eyes, ear tufts and a dark border to the facial disc.
Grey-brown, with fine barring and light blotching below.
Dark brown above, with prominent ear tufts.
The underside in flight is not described.
The rufous morph has orange-yellow eyes and fine barring below.

calls.description: The male calls 'hu-hooo' and the female 'hu-hu-hooo', rising on the second syllable. A grade A file from Kruger near Pafuri is named as an African Wood Owl, so it was not used. The selected file is a grade A call from Grahamstown. The filename is XC252807-Spotted eagle-owls.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a very common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. Grey-brown is not stored as one back colour. The rufous morph's eyes are orange-yellow, so that colour is not stored as one vocabulary name. The highest-ranked Kruger recording is named as an African Wood Owl and was not used. The iNaturalist account has no display name, so the login pgtz is credited. The Kemp name Spotted Eagle Owl and the code RB were left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^8=256 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 128–512.
